rows.anchor: Default `fill-opacity` for a thematic polygon over a basemap: **0.35**
rows.note: The demo rests at 0.42/0.44, not the 0.35 default; 0.35-0.5 is the documented raster band. The executable rule only forbids 1.0.

rows.anchor: On hover it may rise to **0.65**
rows.note: Hover is a state, not a restyle: inline SVG style so CSS can transition it.
Only the district hover uses the 140/200 tokens; buttons and panels still have no motion.

rows.anchor: The boundary layer is above the fill layer
rows.note: Eight named panes are actually used (districts/boundary/casing/route/glow/sites/labels/selection). Before this round every business layer sat in overlayPane, so the pane-based opaque-fill rule inspected an empty pane. Measured: 6 fills, 6 boundaries, 12 glows, 12 cores per direction.

rows.anchor: The boundary is a **separate line layer**
rows.note: The fill polygons are stroke:false; a separate polyline in the boundary pane (411) draws the outline above the fill pane (410). Hover widens it to 2.5px in the accent. The boundary colour is a tuned theme token; a 25%-lighter fallback is computed by lighten().

rows.anchor: Two layers, not one:
rows.note: Each site now has a translucent 10-16px glow in pane 435 plus a crisp core whose radius still carries throughput. The glow is non-interactive and carries a 0.8px blur.

rows.anchor: **The core.**
rows.note: The core keeps a 1px-or-more outline so overlapping points do not merge.

rows.anchor: `essential` is a Mapbox/MapLibre option and **does not exist in Leaflet**
rows.note: The zoom actions use Leaflet flyTo with duration 1.6s, shortened to 0.25s under prefers-reduced-motion. The instant animate:false pans inside selectSite / revealAboveSheet are boundary corrections, which the guidance explicitly allows.

rows.anchor: The blur needs a backdrop to blur
rows.note: The legend card and the compass are floating HUD panels with a translucent ground (alpha 0.92-0.94, kept above 0.9 so contrast is measured against the HUD surface) and a 16px backdrop blur.

rows.anchor: A map is the page.
rows.note: The fixed 272px column still exists for intent, layers and the site list, but the legend and the compass now live on the canvas. The demo is a hybrid, not a pure floating-HUD composition.

rows.anchor: The legend is part of the map
rows.note: The legend is grouped into line/site, value classes and no-data, states the unit, the ramp direction, the class breaks and the count per class. It is collapsible with a 44px control and folds automatically when a popup would overlap it.

rows.anchor: A map is not the interface
rows.note: Three different north indicators: a thin-line rose (operations), a dashed seal with a serif north character (city guide), and a 24-tick instrument dial (monitoring). They state 000 degrees rather than pretending to be bearing instruments.

rows.anchor: Coordinate overlays and side panels
rows.note: Leaflet's transformed mapPane traps every pane in one stacking context, so a popup can never layer above a sibling HUD. The demo measures the intersection and folds the legend instead, then restores it on popupclose.

rows.anchor: These scales are perceptually ordered and tested.
rows.note: The three palettes are exported from their ES modules and measured with the shipped validator's CIEDE2000 / deuteranopia / WCAG functions. All ramps, class pairs, context surfaces and text contrasts now clear the thresholds; output/theme-measurements.json.

rows.anchor: Every figure the reader compares
rows.note: Found by the browser rule in an earlier round and fixed.

rows.anchor: The close button has a hit area of at least 32 by 32 pixels
rows.note: Found only after a popup was actually opened in the regression gate; the engine selector is more specific, so the fix has to match it.

rows.anchor: The class breaks are computed from the data and shown in the legend
rows.note: Breaks are fixed per direction, not computed at runtime; the legend does state them. The demo comment claiming otherwise was corrected.

rows.anchor: These scales are perceptually ordered and tested.
rows.note: The demo uses self-authored ramps; DESIGN-NOTES.md now states why (4 classes, three different grounds) and states each ramp's direction. CIEDE2000 separability is still unmeasured, so this is documentation compliance, not a tested scale.

rows.anchor: The attribution.
rows.note: A named source is present on the map, independent of the optional raster layer.

rows.anchor: Make the judgement executable
rows.note: ?site=S01 opens a popup on load, so popup-covers-feature is actually evaluated instead of being SKIP at every width.

rows.anchor: A taste that cannot be stated as a rule cannot be checked
rows.note: 26 browser + 9 static rules each have a violation fixture and a compliant fixture; the record is output/rule-coverage.json.
